pages.text: From erectus a rock in each hand is not enough. Lash four sticks into a frame and stretch a hide over it - four sticks in your hand, the hide in the other, and $(k:hominin_evolution.item_interact) - and you have somewhere to sit and work stone properly.

Sit at it with two of a stone in hand and a hammerstone and a bone somewhere about you. The hammerstone does the rough shaping; the bone takes the fine flakes off.$(br2)$(l)Hand axe$() - chops wood at last.$(br)$(l)Cleaver$() - a knife that lasts.$(br)$(l)Multitool$() - both, for four stones.
Every tool comes out somewhere from $(l)tier 4$(), crude, to $(l)tier 0$(), flawless. Better tools last longer, hit harder and cut deeper.$(br2)Two things decide it: your hands, and the stone.

Your knapping skill runs from level 4 to level 1, and your journal shows it. One tool takes you off 4; two more off 3; three more off 2. Turning a good stone or a good tool over in your mind sometimes teaches the hands as well.

Limestone is only ever crude. Quartzite gets no better than rough, unless your hands are the best there are. Chert, in a master's hands, can be flawless. Obsidian flakes so cleanly that even a beginner gets a strong edge - and a master may get a perfect one.
